name: pjmpoff
finding: REVIEW_Aug4 A4-C02 (direct far-transfer target offset vs limit: the rejected transfer must install NOTHING)
transitions: real->protected (CR0.PE 0->1, CS far-jump to 32-bit flat code 0x08)
GDT (5 entries): code0 0x08 flat, data0 0x10 flat, code32 0x18 (base 0xF0000, limit 0x8000), code16 0x20 (base 0xF0000, limit 0x0040, D=0)

case (1): direct far JMP ptr16:32 to 0x18:0x8001 (offset = limit+1) -> #GP(0) delivered in the SOURCE context: the handler records vector 13, error code 0, pushed CS = 0x08 (the SOURCE selector, not the rejected 0x18), pushed EIP = the ljmp, and reads back the GDT descriptor high dword INDEXED BY THE PUSHED CS (0x00CF9A00 = the flat source descriptor); skips the 7-byte ljmp and IRETs

case (2): same-privilege far RETF to 0x18:0x8000 (offset == limit, BOUNDARY SUCCESS): the transfer succeeds, the one-byte marker lret at 0x18:0x8000 pops a second fabricated frame back to the flat mainline; ESP stashed before the pushes equals ESP after the round-trip
case (3): direct far JMP to 0x18:0x8000 (offset == limit, BOUNDARY SUCCESS): transfers, the same marker lret returns through a fabricated frame; no #GP in either oracle
case (4): 16-bit variant -- opsize-16 far JMP (66 EA, ptr16:16) to code16 0x20 (D=0, limit 0x0040) offset 0x0041 = limit+1 -> #GP(0), source-context witnesses as case (1)

witnesses.0x2004: 0x00000000 -- case (1) error code (#GP(0)); folded into the ebx composite
witnesses.0x2008: 0x00000008 -- case (1) PUSHED CS = the SOURCE code selector (esi at exit). With the A4-C02 defect the commit arm had already scheduled the target CS, so the frame reads 0x18
witnesses.0x200c: case (1) pushed EIP = the ljmp's linear address (the fault context is the source transfer instruction)
witnesses.0x2010: 0x00CF9A00 -- GDT descriptor high dword read back via the pushed-CS index (ebp at exit): the FLAT source descriptor. The defect reads back the target's 0x00409A0F
witnesses.0x2024: ESP after case (2)'s boundary-RETF round-trip (== 0x2014; folded into the ebx composite)
witnesses.0x2034: 0x00000000 -- case (4) error code; folded into the ebx composite
witnesses.0x2038: 0x00000008 -- case (4) PUSHED CS = the SOURCE selector (ecx at exit)
witnesses.0x203c: case (4) pushed EIP = the 66 EA ljmp's linear address
witnesses.0x2044: scratch: the current case index for the shared #GP handler
witnesses.exit_ebx: 0xB0B0B0B0 iff case-(1) err == 0 AND case-(4) err == 0 AND case-(2) ESP round-tripped exactly (0x2014 == 0x2024)

oracle_gaps.retf_offset_check: QEMU 8.2.2's helper_ret_protected (target/i386/tcg/seg_helper.c) has NO return-EIP-vs-limit check -- neither RETF nor IRET (piretgp0's oracle gap 1 is the IRET half). A same-privilege RETF with offset = limit+1 TRANSFERS SUCCESSFULLY under QEMU where the SDM (and the fixed RTL) raises #GP(0), so the FAULTING-RETF variant of this finding is NOT differentially testable: the two oracles produce genuinely different flows (RTL faults at the retf with ESP preserved; QEMU pops, installs the target CS, and runs on). Case (2) therefore pins the RETF commit path on its LEGAL boundary (offset == limit) differentially; the ESP-preservation property of a REJECTED retf is already pinned differentially by pretfres (H-02, not-present CS). The faulting-RETF offset-vs-limit check itself is RTL-vs-SDM only. Verified 2026-08-04 by reading the pinned QEMU source: the only new_eip-vs-limit checks in seg_helper.c are helper_ljmp_protected (line ~1429), the call-gate branch (~1516), and helper_lcall_protected (~1629); helper_ret_protected has none.
oracle_gaps.fetch_past_limit: QEMU 8.2.2 has no instruction-fetch limit check in translate.c (pfetchlim documents this), and the default RTL TB build compiles out both fetch checks (VEN_SEG_ENFORCE off), so executing the one-byte marker lret AT offset == limit is clean in both oracles. The transfer-time check (this finding) is a separate mechanism present in both.

description: REVIEW_Aug4 A4-C02 regression for direct far-transfer target-offset-vs-limit commit ordering. A direct far JMP (or same-privilege far RETF) to a VALID code segment whose target OFFSET exceeds the segment limit must raise #GP(0) with NOTHING installed: the rejected target's CS base/limit/attributes, CPL and hidden cache never become live, and the fault context is the source transfer instruction. The defect scheduled the CS/CPL/EIP commit writes before the offset check, delivering the #GP from the partially installed target state (handler runs with the target CS, the frame pushes the target CS). This image drives four cases from flat CPL0 code in one run: (1) ljmp ptr16:32 to a limit-0x8000 code32 segment at offset 0x8001 -> #GP(0), the handler proving the SOURCE context via the pushed frame CS/EIP, the zero error code, and a pushed-CS-indexed GDT descriptor read-back; (2) same-privilege RETF at offset == limit, a BOUNDARY SUCCESS whose fabricated-frame round-trip also proves ESP is popped exactly once (QEMU lacks the faulting-RETF limit check -- see oracle_gaps -- so the legal boundary is the differentially testable RETF case); (3) ljmp at offset == limit, BOUNDARY SUCCESS landing on a one-byte marker lret pinned at linear 0xF8000 (image offset 0x8000) that returns through a fabricated frame; (4) the 16-bit variant: an opsize-16 ljmp (66 EA ptr16:16) to a D=0 code16 segment (limit 0x0040) at offset 0x0041 -> #GP(0). QEMU's helper_ljmp_protected checks new_eip > limit BEFORE loading the segment cache, so it is an exact oracle for cases (1)/(3)/(4); the discriminating witnesses are pulled into edi/esi/ebp/ebx/ecx before the isa-debug-exit so the step-7 RTL sys-diff compares them record-for-record. NO paging (the commit-ordering defect is paging-independent).
